Duplicate of the 2409 case: the SSL3 message-type switch is followed by the same shared Unknown fallback.

cr_flush_out's if/else-if enumerate AGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK and any other nonzero io_error; success falls through to the tlswritten==0 check.

else-if only chooses between two independent CA sources; if neither is set, the empty root store build failure downstream catches it, not silently ignored.

get_peer_type's if/else-if only recognize IPv4/IPv6 literals; the fallback CURL_SSL_PEER_DNS return after the if-block handles every remaining hostname.
else-if(!done) only defers on an incomplete deferred connect; the remaining case (done && !result) falls through to the DEBUGASSERT and continues, correctly.
Same deferred-connect pattern in ssl_cf_recv.

else-if(ssl_peer_key) only attempts a secondary hash-based match; if absent, the for-loop continues to the next cached peer, correctly.
else-if only chooses between two independent scache sources; if neither is set, scache stays NULL and no-cache is the correct caller-visible behavior.
else-if(clientcert mismatch) returns FALSE only on mismatch; a match falls through to the shared SRP checks and final return TRUE.
NO_FILESYSTEM else-if only errors when peer verification is required and no CTX callback was set; normal file-based cert loading or disabled verification is unaffected.
Mirrors the openssl/gtls shutdown pattern: the remaining case (peer alive) falls through to sending our own close notify, as intended.

else-if(!result && skiplen) only adjusts the reported write count for a workaround; the general case falls through to the shared return result?-1:nwritten statement.
else-if only sets peer_closed on EOF, same pattern as the gtls/rustls read callbacks.

else-if(!nread) only short-circuits when nothing was read; a normal nread>0 falls through to the encode/queue logic below.
else-if(n==0) only detects a closed connection; n>0 falls through to continue processing the newly received bytes.
The remaining case (frame decoded but nothing written back, e.g. an auto-answered PING) correctly loops to read the next frame.
ws_dec_read_head's state machine handles head_len==0/1 explicitly; head_len>=2 is handled by the unconditional code following the if-block, not by this chain.
else-if(buflen || !remain) only decides whether to forward a chunk; the remaining case (buflen==0 && remain>0) correctly means nothing to forward yet.
else-if(result) catches every decode error; success falls through to loop again, correctly.

Any curl_url_get failure other than out-of-memory is intentionally treated as scheme unknown, later sentineled to '?' so it never matches a protocol check, per the function's own comment.

else-if only chooses a default proxy CRLFILE from the main crlfile; if neither is set, no CRLFILE option needs setting.

else-if only short-circuits two skip-this-redraw optimizations; the remaining case falls through to actually redraw the progress bar.

The trailing-byte-detection else-if only checks known multi-byte lead-byte patterns; a byte matching neither is correctly treated as not a partial UTF-8 sequence.
Same defensive UTF-8 partial-sequence detection one level deeper; unmatched cases are correctly treated as not a 4-byte sequence.
The reserved-device-name else-if(p[x]) no-match/continue case leaves the exact-match case (p[x]=='\\0') to fall through to the following '_' prefix-insertion code, the intended handling.
setfiletime's else-if only clamps the two out-of-range cases; a normal in-range filetime needs no clamping.

The noflagged/expand else-if chain's remaining case (neither applies) correctly falls through to normal option parsing below.
The main parse loop's else-if(!err && passarg) only decides whether to skip the next argv slot; the remaining case correctly needs no extra action here.
GetSizeParameter's else-if(rc) catches every non-overflow parse error; success (rc==0) falls through to the following unit/precision parsing.
Windows getpass_r's else-if('\\b') only handles the backspace-erase special case; a normal keypress correctly falls through to loop again.
else-if(!category[2]) only resolves a single-character short option; a multi-character argument leaves `a` NULL, correctly reported as an unknown option afterward.
This else-if is the final arm of tool_help's own category dispatch and already contains its own fallback (prints Unknown category... and lists categories) for an unmatched category.
else-if(!strcmp(*builtin,\http\")) is a search loop for the http entry to anchor ipfs/ipns insertion; other protocol names correctly just continue the loop unmarked."

customrequest_helper's else-if chain only prints advisory notes for two specific method spellings; any other custom method correctly needs no advisory message.
setup_outfile's else-if(result) catches every remaining error from get_url_file_name; success falls through to continue filling in the output filename below.

Same else-if(result) exhaustive-error pattern for the glob_match_url call.

single_transfer's else-if(SetHTTPrequest(...)) catches every failure from setting the HTTP request type; success falls through to the following httpgetfields handling.
retrycheck's switch(response) intentionally whitelists only the specific transient HTTP status codes that should trigger a retry; any other status code correctly leaves retry as RETRY_NO.
retrycheck's overall if/else-if chain (timeout codes, connrefused, OK-or-failed-http, else if(result)) is exhaustive over all CURLcode outcomes once combined with the OK-checking branch above it.

post_check_result's else-if(FAIL_WITH_BODY) only adds a special-case return for one config mode; other combinations correctly fall through to returning the original result unchanged.

On Windows, post_per_transfer's `if(per->uploadfile) {...} else if(per->infdopen) curlx_close(per->infd);` only closes the raw upload fd when per->uploadfile is unset, but per->uploadfile is also truthy for a regular (non-stdin) uploaded file whose fd was opened via curlx_open() and marked infdopen=TRUE earlier in this same file (lines 264-291); so on Windows a real file upload's descriptor is never closed here, and grepping the codebase finds no other close call for it -- a plausible per-transfer file descriptor leak.
urlerr_cvt's if/else-if chain is followed by an unconditional return CURLE_URL_MALFORMAT that serves as the exhaustive default for every unmatched CURLUcode.
The switch(action) fully enumerates every value of the 3-member enum e_action (allow/deny/set) it switches on, so there is no unhandled value; a default label would be dead code.
get_line's else-if(feof(input)) only recognizes end-of-file as a valid line terminator; the remaining case (partial line, more data expected) correctly falls through to read more.
unslashquote's else-if(curlx_dyn_addn(...)) return 1 only handles the out-of-memory/too-long error from appending a literal character; success falls through to loop again.
The download-total-tallying else-if(!per->dltotal_added) only prevents double-counting; if already counted, correctly nothing further is needed.
Same double-counting guard for the upload total.
max5data's else-if(nbytes<10000) only picks a no-decimal format for a mid-size range; the remaining (still too large) case correctly falls through to scale up and loop again.
glob_set's else-if(size>=palloc) only grows the element array when full; the remaining case (space still available) correctly needs no reallocation.

read_variable's else-if(ge) only assigns content from the environment for import; the remaining case (a default-value action was specified, env var unset) correctly falls through to that default-value handling later in the function.
